referents.why: third masculine singular suffix on 'say to him'; the command just before is 'go to Pharaoh', so the one Moses is to speak to is Pharaoh
referents.category: pronoun picks up the destination of a preceding command

referents.why: first person singular 'my' inside the messenger speech opened by 'thus says Yahweh'; the speaker of that speech is the LORD (w14), not Moses
referents.category: first person inside a relayed speech

referents.why: first person singular 'me' in the same relayed speech; the purpose is that they serve the one whose speech this is, the LORD
referents.category: first person inside a relayed speech

referents.why: second masculine singular imperative 'go' in the LORD's speech to Moses (cl0 addressee)
referents.category: implied subject of a command in the outer speech

referents.why: second masculine singular weqatal 'you will say' continues the command to Moses in the outer speech; the clause introduces the inner speech but belongs to the outer one
referents.category: implied subject of a command that introduces a commanded speech

referents.why: second masculine singular imperative 'let go' sits inside the speech Moses is to say; its addressee is Pharaoh, whom Moses is sent to (cl1, cl2 'to him'), not Moses
referents.category: implied subject of a command inside a commanded speech

referents.why: third masculine plural 'they may serve' after 'let my people go'; the plural agrees with the collective 'people' and the sense is that the people serve
referents.category: implied subject of a purpose clause referring to the object of the command

links.why: a clause linked to itself; the opening wayyiqtol has no earlier clause in this verse to continue (the previous verse is the episode rung, not a within-verse then)
weqatal 'and you will say' follows 'go' and continues it as the next step of the same errand, same second person
waw + yiqtol in a different person (you to they) after a command is a purpose, not a plain 'and'
links.category: plain and read where a change of person gives purpose

links.why: command 'let my people go', then waw + yiqtol third plural 'that they may serve me': a different person, so what the release is for
links.category: command then waw plus yiqtol in a different person

links.why: 'he said' and what was said: the run of commands 'go ... and you will say' joined by and at one level, so the content is the whole imperative group
links.category: speech clause and its commanded content

links.why: 'you will say to him' and what Moses is to say, 'thus says Yahweh ...'; the content is the whole inner turn (frame cl3 with its message), not its frame clause cl3 alone, so I point at the group rather than at cl3
links.category: command to speak and the embedded speech it introduces

links.why: 'thus says Yahweh' is the messenger formula; what the LORD says is the command 'let my people go' with its purpose, held as one imperative group
links.category: messenger formula and the message it carries

groups.why: the LORD speaks to Moses; the parts are the commands (imp1) and the turn Moses is commanded to give (g1), replacing the bare clause parts cl1 and cl2 so the nesting shows
groups.category: outer turn holding a commanded turn

groups.why: 'go' and 'and you will say' are commands at one level to the same person; cl2 is second person, so it is a second command, not an effect (an effect would be a third-person weqatal)
groups.category: commands joined by and, second weqatal is a command not an effect

groups.why: Moses is told to say something to Pharaoh: this turn is the commanded one, framed by 'you will say to him', whose part is what is to be said (turn1)
groups.category: commanded turn between a sender and a third party

groups.why: 'thus says Yahweh' frames the message; the speech is the LORD's word, delivered to Pharaoh through Moses; the bare parts cl4 and cl5 are replaced by their imperative group, and the addressee Pharaoh is added
groups.category: relayed speech with the original sender and the final addressee

groups.why: 'let my people go' is the command; 'that they may serve me' is waw + yiqtol in a different person, an aim, not a second command
groups.category: command with an aim in a different person
